experiment_design.technical_details: This experimental design tests the hypothesis that dendritic cell (DC) uptake of apoptotic material is a primary negative feedback regulator maintaining immune homeostasis. The study utilizes a murine model with conditional knockout of key phagocytic receptors (e.g., MerTK or Axl) specifically in CD11c+ DCs to block apoptotic cargo uptake without inducing general inflammation. We will employ flow cytometry and confocal microscopy to quantify apoptotic cargo uptake rates in steady-state vs. perturbed conditions. Longitudinal profiling of serum cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha, IL-10) and autoantibody titers (ANA) will assess loss of dynamic equilibrium. Reversibility will be tested by administering apoptotic cell infusions to restore uptake capacity. The protocol adheres to strict sterile techniques and blinded analysis to minimize bias.

experiment_design.methods: 1. **Model Generation**: Generate MerTK-floxed mice crossed with CD11c-Cre transgenics to achieve DC-specific deletion of the apoptotic sensor MerTK. Controls include littermate MerTK-fl/fl mice without Cre. 2. **In Vitro Uptake Assay**: Isolate BMDCs and incubate with pHrodo-labeled apoptotic thymocytes. Quantify uptake via flow cytometry to validate blockade efficiency. 3. **In Vivo Homeostasis Challenge**: Monitor cohorts (n=10 per group) over 12 weeks under steady-state conditions. Collect blood samples bi-weekly. 4. **Perturbation & Reversal**: At week 6, administer a controlled dose of apoptotic cells intravenously to a subset of KO mice to test if restoring cargo availability rescues homeostatic markers. 5. **Omics Profiling**: Perform RNA-seq on splenic DCs at baseline and week 12 to identify downstream tolerogenic signaling pathways (e.g., IDO1, TGF-beta expression).

baselines: Wild-type C57BL/6 mice (normal DC uptake function)
MerTK-fl/fl mice without Cre (genetic control for floxed allele)
CD11c-Cre mice without floxed MerTK (control for Cre toxicity)
metrics: Mean Fluorescence Intensity (MFI) of pHrodo-labeled apoptotic cargo in DCs
Serum concentration of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha) via ELISA
Anti-nuclear antibody (ANA) titer as a marker of auto-reactivity
Frequency of FoxP3+ regulatory T cells in spleen and lymph nodes
experiments.ablation: Compare MerTK-KO DCs vs. Axl-KO DCs to determine if redundancy exists between phosphatidylserine receptors. If Axl-KO shows no phenotype while MerTK-KO does, it suggests MerTK is the dominant sensor for this homeostatic loop.
experiments.validation_protocol: Blinded analysis of flow cytometry data by two independent researchers. Statistical significance determined by two-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post-hoc test for multiple comparisons. Power analysis conducted to ensure n=10 provides 80% power to detect a 20% change in cytokine levels.

experiment_design.technical_details: This experimental design tests the hypothesis that dendritic cell (DC) uptake of apoptotic material is a primary negative feedback regulator maintaining immune homeostasis. The study utilizes a murine model with conditional knockout of key phagocytic receptors (e.g., MerTK or Axl) specifically in CD11c+ DCs to block apoptotic cargo uptake without inducing general inflammation. We will employ flow cytometry and confocal microscopy to quantify apoptotic cargo uptake rates in steady-state vs. perturbed conditions. Longitudinal profiling of serum cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha, IL-10) and autoantibody titers (ANA) will assess loss of dynamic equilibrium. Reversibility will be tested by administering apoptotic cell infusions to restore uptake capacity. The protocol adheres to strict sterile techniques and blinded analysis to minimize bias.
